business_model: Two-sided peer-to-peer accommodation marketplace, take-rate on bookings

historical_evidence.company: Founded 2008 by Brian Chesky, Joe Gebbia, and Nathan Blecharczyk, a marketplace connecting travelers with hosts renting spare rooms or entire homes.
historical_evidence.market: Large global travel-accommodation market with an established, heavily-regulated incumbent structure (hotels), and genuine open regulatory/legitimacy questions about short-term residential rentals in many jurisdictions as of 2011 — a real, contemporaneously-known risk factor, not a hindsight-informed one.
historical_evidence.team: Founding team had operated the company for roughly three years by the snapshot date, through Y Combinator and a prior, smaller Series A.
historical_evidence.product: Two-sided marketplace product connecting hosts and guests, with recent expansion (via acquisition of a German competitor) strengthening its European footprint shortly before this round.
historical_evidence.execution: Raised $112M in Series B funding in July 2011, led by Andreessen Horowitz (contributing $60M of the total) with DST Global and General Catalyst participating, at a $1.3 billion valuation — a large step-up from its prior Series A ($7.2M), and Airbnb's formal entry into the 'unicorn' valuation tier.
historical_evidence.traction: Reported having surpassed one million total bookings worldwide within roughly the preceding four months as of the snapshot — a real, disclosed usage-scale figure, not merely a funding-size signal.
historical_evidence.financial: No specific revenue or take-rate figures were found in the contemporaneous sources reviewed for the July 2011 snapshot.

normalized_facts.source: TechCrunch / CNN Money / Airbnb press release
